notes.src/civilization/simulation.js: Re-baselined in v13 for geography-driven district names, and again for biome 21: the two forest tests ([7,8,9,10,11]) had to learn the subtropical laurel forest, or a settlement standing in one would read its hinterland as treeless. Locked by the settlementFingerprint assertion in tests/onemap.test.mjs. Re-baselined again for state formation, deliberately this time. The administration step cost now treats mountain walls and river fords as real barriers rather than a mild surcharge, so a frontier falls on something you can point at; each founding council draws its reach from a long tail before the land search rather than after, so realms range from one province to forty-six instead of all being middling; and nameRealms() names a realm for the legend, landform, volcano or plate it holds rather than for its capital. physicalFingerprint and settlementFingerprint are unchanged and still asserted; politicalFingerprint moves because the borders themselves are the change. Re-baselined for mythological realm namebases: founding and secession now use RealmNames; custom names clear generated provenance. Naming has its own random stream. Initial terrain, settlement and border fingerprints remain 440ae5d0 / 6b6c5ea8 / aaa577eb; founding diplomacy draws now follow the territorial pass directly, so newly generated histories can differ from older versions. Existing saved histories retain their names and state. Re-baselined for connected sovereignty with local administration, fewer founding councils, and geographically rooted population majorities. This deliberately changes new political histories (d8ba763d), preserving physical 440ae5d0, settlements 6b6c5ea8, every full-precision population/settlement record and the province raster across three seeds; old saves retain their stored borders and mixtures. tests/polity-coverage.test.mjs verifies those invariants, minority populations, connected claims, direct-administration budgets and save continuation. Re-baselined for rare high-altitude cities: at most two supported settlements above 3,500 m transfer existing rural residents and retained rural capacity into tiny urban courts. Existing ordinary settlements, their size, cultures and founding borders remain unchanged; total population and capacity are conserved. The default settlement fingerprint intentionally changes from 6b6c5ea8 to e6aee7b8; physical/political fingerprints remain 440ae5d0 / d8ba763d. High-citadel site tests compare all ordinary provinces and founding politics directly with founding disabled. Older saved histories retain their founding version on history or politics rerolls. Re-baselined for version 2 high citadel founding on the versioned landforms. Only newly generated landformVersion 1 worlds default to this rule: after ordinary cultures and countries form, up to two existing owned rural provinces establish tiny settlements on real dry platforms above 3500 m within their unchanged cell lists. Local population and retained rural carrying capacity fund them; no physical raster, province ownership, cultural mixture, administration graph or ordinary town changes. Initial settlement records include the new sites. Explicit saved founding versions 0/1 retain their original behavior and legacy fingerprints. tests/high-citadel-platforms.test.mjs checks the current default world, exact ordinary-city layout parity, original politics, budgets, save replay and bounded growth; tests/high-citadel-sites.test.mjs retains the version 1 locks.
notes.src/world/geography.js: Re-baselined three times. (a) Legendary places: nameLegends() writes only w.legends. (b) Two landform priors — irregular basin depressions and collision-belt plateaus. (c) Biomes 21 and 22, the subtropics: every humid cell from 7 to 21 C used to be called temperate, so a laurel forest at 19 C and a beech wood at 11 C carried the same two words and grew the same tree. Appended, never inserted, because the indices below are written into saves and into every biome test here. (b) and (c) move the world by design: physicalFingerprint dfd91476 -> 4b02963c -> 440ae5d0, settlementFingerprint 77c3b21f -> 73c1127f -> 6b6c5ea8, all asserted at the current values in tests/onemap.test.mjs and tests/climate.test.mjs. Re-baselined for versioned regional bedrock sculpting: new worlds opt into landformVersion 1, with connected red tablelands and branching canyons, folded mountain belts, basalt calderas and limestone towers before the final drainage and climate solve. The coastline, prescribed basins and fjords are protected. Missing/zero versions retain every legacy physical raster byte across three seeds, including physical 440ae5d0, while old saved histories keep their original terrain. tests/fantasy-landforms.test.mjs measures actual geometry, hydrology, exposed feature anchors and deterministic replay; the integration and browser checks cover cities, political continuity, worker parity and both save versions. Version 2 replaces evenly spaced folded crests with tectonically oriented massifs and a branching ridge network, followed by the same ocean, moisture, glacier and drainage calculations. Version 1 remains byte-compatible for published saves, alongside version 0. Mountain morphology tests reject periodic comb-like height fields, and controlled climate counterfactuals check lapse-rate cooling, windward precipitation, lee-side moisture depletion and ocean-current influence.
notes.src/render/world-renderer.js: Re-baselined for two deliberate rendering changes. (a) Map clarity: supersampled backing store in resize(), Geometry.smoothTri() for per-vertex terrain normals and colours, buildLegends() markers. (b) Political layers: realms and diplomacy no longer paint a country's territory at all. Every border already carries a cased frontier line, and that is the whole of the country on this map; only the realm you have selected takes a faint wash, so the selection is answerable. Faiths, peoples, wealth and magic keep their full colour, where the colour is the measurement. Terrain vertex positions are untouched: the surface is locked by AtlasSpace.surface parity and the shared-edge check in tests/continuous.test.mjs, and the political palette by the coverage assertion in tests/onemap.test.mjs. The v12 shader and layer-visibility normalisations are folded into this baseline. Re-baselined again for the climate pass: buildSymbols() draws climate-driven vegetation (seven forms from CityEnvironment.canopy, with a treeline) via the shared plantForm() helper. Terrain, rivers, ice, dunes, volcanoes, camera, picking, legends and the shadow pipeline are unchanged. Also carries the two subtropical tree silhouettes, laurel and hardleaf, added with biomes 21 and 22. Two further rendering changes: the volcano symbol is gone — a vent's cone is already in w.height, so it drew a second schematic cone on top of the real mountain — and plantForm takes a coarse detail flag for the scatter that fills a whole visible landscape. Re-baselined again for Geometry.tri, which is now allocation-free: it had been building seven throwaway arrays and four spreads per triangle, about 3.6M allocations for a single town, and that was most of the wait after clicking into one. The arithmetic is unchanged down to the use of Math.hypot, so every vertex is bit-identical and the geometry-hash assertions across the suite pass untouched, which is what pins it. The city coherence fix enables slope-scaled polygon offset only during the shadow depth pass, removing diagonal self-shadow stripes on close terrain. Terrain geometry and physical simulation remain unchanged. Re-baselined for the selected ground marker: radius, stroke and lift are capped in CSS pixels and refreshed when camera scale changes. World terrain and picking are unchanged. Re-baselined for PR #36 river detail: buildLines delegates to buildRivers so the near river surface can refine independently of unrelated overlays; the world-map river representation is preserved. The nearby vegetation scale fix also keeps coarse alpine cushions as low as their full-detail form and suppresses treeless/nonpositive-height plant geometry. tests/tree-scale.test.mjs checks all 11 forms, actual town and landscape meshes, fixed city layout/tree hashes and unchanged world/simulation data; tests/river-detail.test.mjs checks drainage, width and refinement. Geography and civilization byte locks are unchanged. Map loading optimization reuses a single Float32 vertex array for GPU upload, picking and export. No arithmetic, vertex count or visual detail changes; tests/city-collection.test.mjs checks byte-identical continuous meshes, worker/fallback transfers and buffer views, and original-main mesh hashes were compared for three cities. Re-baselined for country-label hover: a temporary territory wash and cased outline follow current province ownership, including owned glaciers and excluding water. Hover keeps the selected country and camera unchanged; leaving restores the original selected or measurement palette. Realm hover tests cover restoration, ownership changes and world/layer replacement. The continuous map recolours its existing terrain buffer without remeshing or invalidating shadows; its baseline colours restore exactly on leave. Terrain positions and simulation data are unchanged. National borders now also draw dashed boundaries against unclaimed dry land in either scan direction, including the last raster row and column; coast and lake water stay untouched. tests/political-land.test.mjs checks actual border geometry. Re-baselined for biome surface detail: terrain-only shadow polygon offset now spans the full PCF footprint on steep faces. Building shadow offsets and physical terrain inputs stay unchanged. Re-baselined for inland lake sovereignty: a separate read-only shoreline partition extends national borders, hover outlines and selected-country washes across inland water. Enclosed domestic lakes no longer make holes; shared lakes retain a continuous frontier. Water palettes, physical geometry and inhabited province accounting stay unchanged. Political-land, real-lake integration and hover-buffer tests cover live ownership, cache invalidation and exact colour restoration. Re-baselined for complete sovereign territory: all positive-height dry land and inland lakes participate in country borders and hover, including outlying ice, desert and islands. Derived ownership does not modify province administration, population, physical geography or measurement values. Complete-territory tests cover four worlds, total land-area shares and remote terrain highlights. Re-baselined for domestic holes: closed below-sea-level water components now participate in sovereign borders and hover without being cut out as ocean. Open ocean and open wildness remain unclaimed, while enclosed domestic land and water belong to their surrounding country. Foreign enclaves retain inner borders. Physical terrain and province accounting are unchanged.
notes.src/city/generator.js: Version 2 mountain courts have a fixed 0.648-cell precinct. They are excluded from the ordinary cityReach spacing upper bound, so adding a remote tiny court cannot shrink an existing town survey. Version 1 spacing remains unchanged. The current-default regression compares every ordinary survey and the full nearest-city layout hash with high founding disabled; its terrain, streets, architecture and vegetation stay identical.
